question: What explains the decision to postpone AUTODIN II's transition to standard TCP/IP until after initial operational capability? Test cost, schedule, compatibility, technical readiness, and contractual commitments against the records.

new_chronology_entries.event: SRI International Proposal for Research No. ECU 79-99, the NIC follow-on proposal to DCA. Its technical part contains Task 2, Production of a Protocol Locator, and Task 5, Transition of Information Services from ARPANET to AUTODIN II. The Protocol Locator task describes 1,500 copies whose contents depend on receipt of each official protocol from DCA, NSW or ARPA, covering ARPANET/AUTODIN, NSW and internet protocols, for distribution to bona fide ARPANET, NSW or AUTODIN II users.
new_chronology_entries.source: SRI CHM archives photographs IMG_6472, IMG_6473, IMG_6493, IMG_6501, IMG_6537, IMG_6538, IMG_6540, IMG_6553.
new_chronology_entries.evidence_level: OCR discovery; proposal number and date read on IMG_6501 and IMG_6537

new_chronology_entries.date: undated addendum; associated cost sheet dated 1979-11-05
new_chronology_entries.event: DELETION OF TWO TASKS FROM THE NIC PROPOSAL. 'ADDENDUM TO PROPOSAL ECU 79-99' records that 'As a result of the discussions held between representatives of Defense Communications Agency and SRI, this addendum revises Proposal ECU 79-99', and deletes two tasks in their entirety: 'Task 2, Production of a Protocol Locator (pages 9 and 10)' and 'Task 5: Transition of Information Services from ARPANET to AUTODIN II (page 17)'. In their place a new Sub-task 10 provides online access to ARPANET and FTP protocols, with selection and approval resting on the NWG coordinator, 'currently Jon Postel', or another DCA-appointed representative. Task 3 is reduced to an eight-month period, 1 November 1979 to 30 June 1980.
new_chronology_entries.source: SRI CHM archives IMG_6527, inspected as an image at full resolution. The addendum page carries no date on its face; the revised cost estimates filed with it are headed 'Proposal for Research No. ECU 79-99 ... 5 November 1979' (IMG_6531, also inspected as an image).
new_chronology_entries.kind: contractor proposal revision following discussions with DCA
new_chronology_entries.reading_limit: The undated addendum revises proposed work following DCA/SRI discussions and accompanies dated cost sheets. It does not establish an executed contract change, an exact addendum date, the reason for deletion, or a program-level transition decision.

new_chronology_entries.event: Western Union TCP specification Revision 3 delivered under DCA200-C-637. DTIC report number DCA 200-C-637-P005, secondary number AD-E100 342, FINAL, controlling and monitoring office Defense Communications Agency ATTN: Code 450, 155 pages, unclassified, approved for public release, DTIC stamp 7 MAR 80. Revision 3's list of changed pages is Title, 10, 30, B-1, C-1, C-44, D-4. Printed p. 4, the reference list, is not among them, so the reference list stood unchanged from the March 5, 1979 original issue. That list names ten documents: the NIC TELNET specification, the ARPANET Protocol Handbook, the two SRI specifications of 15 July 1976, the DCA System Performance Specification (Type A) for AUTODIN II Phase I, WU Proposal WU-301-1 of April 1976, the WU AUTODIN II Design Plan and its Executive Summary, and the AUTODIN II THP and SIP Transportable Specifications. No DoD standard protocol document is cited.
new_chronology_entries.source: AD-A081756, Internet Archive item DTIC_ADA081756. DD Form 1473 at PDF p. 5 and the reference list at PDF p. 13 / printed p. 4, both inspected as rendered images and retained in pages/.
new_chronology_entries.significance: The TCP deliverable now matches the THP deliverable exactly on the point that mattered: same contract, same controlling office, same delivery date, and a reference list untouched since early 1979 that cites no DoD standard.

new_chronology_entries.event: SRI Proposal for Research No. ECU 80-149, for the NIC contract year 1 January to 31 December 1981, proposes a NIC Protocol Repository. Its Attachment 1, 'Preliminary List of Protocols to be Maintained in the NIC Protocol Repository', lists two families. Under 'DoD Standard Protocols': Transmission Control Protocol, Internet Protocol, File Transfer Protocol, Mail Service, Telenet/Terminal Handling Protocols, Remote Job Entry, Interactive Graphics, Conferencing, Non-Interactive Graphics, Facsimile, Real Time Protocol, Network Voice Protocols, Multimedia Conferencing, Datagram, Message Protocols. Under 'AUTODIN II Protocols': Segment Interface Protocol, Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), Mode VI Link Protocol, Terminal to Host Protocol (THP), Terminal Access Controller (TAC) Link Protocols. The same proposal's optional tasks ask the NIC to support the DoD Standard Transmission Control and Internet Protocols and to provide configuration management of the DoD Standard Protocol Specifications (Type A) under DoD-STD-480A, DCA-100-50-2 and MIL-STD-483.
new_chronology_entries.source: SRI CHM archives IMG_6612 (inspected as an image), duplicated in draft at IMG_6615; optional tasks at IMG_6605; proposal number and date at IMG_6618, IMG_6632, IMG_6636.
new_chronology_entries.significance: Eight months after the April 3, 1980 ratification, the NIC's own proposed repository still treats the AUTODIN II protocols as a separate family with its own Transmission Control Protocol, distinct from the DoD standard one. This is contemporaneous corroboration that the two branches were still maintained as different things after ratification, consistent with implementation being placed after IOC.
new_chronology_entries.reading_limit: A contractor's preliminary list of documents to hold, not a statement of DCA policy or of the transition schedule.

records_survival_findings.finding: RG 371 has 31 published disposition schedules. The September 13 record worked from one of them, n1-371-87-001, Section LXXVI, AUTODIN II Files. The other thirty were not previously searched.
records_survival_findings.coverage: All 31 retrieved on 2026-09-14 from the NARA index at https://www.archives.gov/records-mgmt/rcs/schedules/index.html?dir=/departments/department-of-defense/defense-agencies/rg-0371 . Search used the files' existing searchable text layers; some are scans with OCR, not native born-digital text. Fingerprints and per-file URLs in text/nara-rg0371/manifest.json.
records_survival_findings.consequence: No dedicated series was identified in this search. Searchable text, terminology and series descriptions limit that negative. General series, other offices and unlisted holdings remain possible; the function cannot be declared unscheduled or its records destroyed from this result.

records_survival_findings.finding: nc1-371-81-01, Section LXXV, ARPANET Files, is new to this brief. It schedules series 875-01 through 875-19 for DCA's operational management of the ARPANET.
permanent: 875-02 ARPANET Sponsors Group Files. Chaired by DCA; representatives of ARPANET sponsors meeting to review and coordinate all actions affecting network services, to coordinate proposed network changes, and to exchange information on network operations and future plans. Includes charter, announcements, agenda, minutes, group reports, recommendations. Disposition: HQ DCA permanent, offer to NARS in five-year blocks when twenty years old.

875-03 ARPANET Operational Management Files. Policies, procedures and standards for operation and maintenance; access criteria for new users; papers governing hardware, software and the Network Control Center; node-to-node and very distant host-to-node leases. Disposition: office of record permanent, same transfer terms.
records_survival_findings.consequence: ARPANET Sponsors Group and operational-management records were scheduled permanent at the specified offices. They are possible routes for related material, not proof that they hold protocol-panel papers or survive today.
records_survival_findings.disposal_instructions: 875-01, 875-04 through 875-19 are all destroy-when-no-longer-needed, destroy-when-superseded, or destroy at 1, 3, 5 or 10 years. 875-13 ARPANET Modernization Program, the Honeywell-to-C/30 replacement, explicitly names a terminal control protocol (TCP) and is destroy when no longer needed at 5 years.

records_survival_findings.finding: nc1-371-78-01, approved February 1978, makes 203-01 Publications Record Set Files permanent — one copy of each publication or change issued by a DCA activity — and 203-02 Publications Background Files permanent, covering 'studies, recommendations, comments, concurrences, and similar documents that provide a basis for the publication or that contribute to its content'.

nc1-371-81-02, Section 829, IAS files, schedules 829-52 IAS Data Handling/Network Design Files, whose contents include 'functional and operational description, protocol, addressing, signaling, and error control', as destroy at 20 years for the office of record.
records_survival_findings.consequence: Recorded as context on how DCA scheduled protocol-bearing engineering files generally: twenty years and destroy, not permanent.
